title: Responding to cyberbullying
examples: If someone is sending mean messages, what is the very first thing I should do?
What is the difference between blocking someone and reporting them?
If I see cyberbullying happen to a friend, what should I do?

explain.say: If someone is being unkind online, you should first tell a trusted adult.

items: Do not keep it a secret

explain.say: Next, you should use the block feature on the app or website.
After blocking, it is important to report the bad behaviour to the platform.
Remember to save evidence before you report or block anything.
If you see something unkind, you can also tell a friend for support.

draw.text: Talk to a friend for support.

explain.say: In real life, if someone says something mean to you at school, you should tell a teacher right away.

faq.q: What is the very first thing I should do if someone is cyberbullying me?
faq.a: You should tell a trusted adult immediately. This could be a parent, teacher, or guardian. You might also ask, 'Who should I tell first?' or 'What is the first step?'
asks: What is the first thing to do?
Who do I talk to first?

faq.q: Should I block the person or report them first?
faq.a: It is best to tell an adult first, and then follow the steps of reporting and blocking. Telling an adult keeps you safe and gets help.
asks: Which is better, blocking or reporting?

faq.q: Do I need to take screenshots?
faq.a: Yes, taking screenshots is very helpful evidence. It shows exactly what was said and when it was said.

faq.q: If I block someone, does it stop them from knowing I blocked them?
faq.a: Blocking stops them from contacting you through that specific platform. However, they might try other ways to reach you.

faq.q: What if the bullying is happening on a game I play?
faq.a: You should still tell an adult and use the game's built-in reporting tools. Most games have safety features you can use.

facts: Always tell a trusted adult about cyberbullying.
Use the block feature to stop unwanted contact.
Use the report feature to let the platform know about bad behaviour.
Taking screenshots helps keep evidence of the bullying.

quiz.say: If someone sends you mean messages online, what is the correct sequence of actions?

options.show: Tell an adult first, then report the content, and finally block the user.
options.say: Tell an adult first, then report the content, and finally block the user.

options.show: Block the user first, then report it.
options.say: Block the user first, then report it.

options.show: Report it, and then tell an adult.
options.say: Report it, and then tell an adult.

options.show: Tell an adult, and then block and report.
options.say: Tell an adult, and then block and report.

quiz.why: Telling an adult first ensures you get immediate support and guidance for the situation.

wrong.1: Blocking first might delete evidence you need for the platform to investigate.
wrong.2: Reporting alone does not guarantee safety, and you need adult support right away.
wrong.3: This order is good, but reporting is usually the next official step after telling.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of using the 'report' function?

options.show: To prove to my friends that they were wrong.
options.say: To prove to my friends that they were wrong.

options.show: To let the website or app moderators see the bad behaviour.
options.say: To let the website or app moderators see the bad behaviour.

options.show: To make the person feel bad.
options.say: To make the person feel bad.

quiz.why: Reporting sends the content to the people who run the site so they can remove it.

wrong.0: The evidence is for the adults and the platform, not just for friends to see.
wrong.2: The goal is safety, not revenge, so reporting is for the platform staff.
wrong.3: Reporting and blocking are two separate actions you must take.

quiz.say: If I am worried about something online, what should I do?

options.show: Delete all the messages right away.
options.say: Delete all the messages right away.

options.show: Talk to a parent or trusted teacher immediately.
options.say: Talk to a parent or trusted teacher immediately.

options.show: Just ignore it and hope it stops.
options.say: Just ignore it and hope it stops.

quiz.why: Adults can help you understand the situation and take the right steps together.

wrong.0: Responding with meanness makes the situation worse and can get you in trouble too.
wrong.1: Deleting them removes the evidence that adults need to help you.
wrong.3: Ignoring it can make you feel worse, and the bullying might continue.
